title: Model switch during a weight read starts a second large load while the cancelled one is still filling memory; the memory gate counts the stale load as releasable
scenario: The user picks Inkling DWQ (9.6 GB). While the bar shows the weight phase, they switch to GPTQ-small (10.45 GB). reconcileSelection() calls inflight?.task.cancel(), sets inflight = nil and bumps epoch. ChatView's .task(id:) then calls load(), which finds no inflight entry for the new epoch and immediately spawns a new performLoad. The cancelled task keeps going: loadWeights runs on DispatchQueue.global inside withCheckedThrowingContinuation and never checks Task cancellation. The two models' weights become resident at the same time (~20 GB on a 16 GB iPad) and jetsam kills the app. MemoryBudget.fit() does not catch this, because heldByModel = MLX activeMemory + cacheMemory includes the stale load's partially resident weights and adds them back to the budget as if a switch would free them. This contradicts the PR claim that two 10 GB loads can't run at once.
evidence: Line 72 has the comment `inflight?.task.cancel()   // stops a download in progress; a weight read finishes and is dropped`, followed by `inflight = nil`. Line 86 is `if let inflight, inflight.epoch == epoch { return (inflight.task, epoch) }`, otherwise a new Task is created. In Vendor/.../MLXLMCommon/Load.swift, the async loadWeights dispatches to DispatchQueue.global(qos: .userInitiated) with no cancellation checks. Line 25 is `heldByModel = { MLX.Memory.activeMemory + MLX.Memory.cacheMemory }`, used in fit() and at line 134.
fix: Keep the cancelled task as `draining`, and have the next load `await draining.value` (ignoring its result or error) before running fit() and starting performLoad. Alternatively, serialize all performLoad calls through one actor or queue so a new load cannot begin until the previous Task has returned and its container is released (then call MLX.Memory.clearCache()).
notes:
UPHELD(medium): I could not refute this claim. I read each cited piece of code on origin/inkling2.

(1) In MLXBackend.swift, reconcileSelection() calls `inflight?.task.cancel()`, sets `inflight = nil` and bumps `epoch`. The comment there admits that "a weight read finishes and is dropped". load() only reuses an inflight task whose epoch matches. Here inflight is nil, so the new load spawns a fresh `Task { performLoad }` right away. Nothing waits for the old task.

(2) The vendored ios/Vendor/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLMCommon/Load.swift has an async loadWeights that runs the synchronous loader inside withCheckedThrowingContinuation on DispatchQueue.global. That loader is loadModelCheckpoint, which uses DispatchQueue.concurrentPerform and evals every tensor range. It has no Task.isCancelled or checkCancellation anywhere, so a cancelled task keeps reading and allocating until the whole model is resident. It also runs materializeModelForInference after that.

(3) The trigger is reachable from the UI. The SettingsView Picker is not disabled while a load runs. Its onChange calls backend.switchModel, and ChatView's `.task(id: selectedModelID)` restarts and calls backend.load. That load runs reconcileSelection, which is a no-op because it already switched, then starts the new performLoad.

(4) The memory gate does not catch it. MemoryBudget.fit() computes the budget as availableBytes plus heldByModel(), and heldByModel is MLX activeMemory + cacheMemory. Both include the stale load's partially resident arrays. Those arrays are not freed by the switch, but the gate counts them as releasable. loadLarge sets memoryLimit from the same inflated number, and that limit is soft anyway.

Result: for Inkling tiers that are already downloaded (DWQ at 9.60 GB resident, GPTQ-small at 10.45 GB), switching during the weight phase overlaps two weight loads of about 10 GB each on a 16 GB iPad, and jetsam kills the app.

Caveat, and why confidence is medium rather than high: if the new model is not downloaded yet, its download (11.5 GB) would almost certainly outlast the stale weight read. The overlap then mostly disappears, so the high-impact case needs both models already cached. That is plausible, since the user can switch between tiers they have used before. I have not run this on a device. | fix: In MLXBackend, keep the cancelled task as `draining: Task<ModelContainer, Error>?` instead of dropping it in reconcileSelection(). At the start of performLoad, or in load() before spawning the new task, do `_ = try? await draining?.value`, then `MLX.Memory.clearCache()`, and only then run MemoryBudget.fit and the load. A simpler alternative: serialize every performLoad through one actor, or chain each new task off the previous one, so a new load cannot start until the previous Task has returned and its container is released. Optionally, also disable the Settings model Picker while a load is in progress.

UPHELD(high): I could not refute this. The code confirms it on origin/inkling2.

1. Cancelling does not wait for the old load. In MLXBackend.swift, reconcileSelection() (lines 66-78) cancels the inflight task, sets inflight to nil and bumps epoch. The comment there admits that "a weight read finishes and is dropped".

2. The next load starts straight away. ChatView.swift's `.task(id: selectedModelID)` re-runs when the model changes and calls load(). In load() (line 86), the inflight check fails because inflight is now nil, so a new Task runs performLoad for the new entry. Nothing waits for the old task to end. The "one load at a time" guarantee only covers callers within the same epoch.

3. The old load keeps reading weights. The vendored ios/Vendor/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLMCommon/Load.swift runs the async loadWeights inside withCheckedThrowingContinuation on DispatchQueue.global, and the sync loader fans out with DispatchQueue.concurrentPerform. Neither one checks Task.isCancelled, so the cancelled read keeps going until it finishes.

4. The memory gate misses it. MemoryBudget.fit() computes budget = os_proc_available_memory() + heldByModel(), where heldByModel = MLX activeMemory + cacheMemory (set at MLXBackend.swift:25). The stale load's resident arrays lower the available memory and raise activeMemory by the same amount, so they cancel out. The gate effectively ignores the old load and passes the new model, e.g. GPTQ-small at 10.45 GB resident (ModelCatalog.swift:93). loadLarge (line 134) sets memoryLimit from the same inflated budget. That limit is only a soft cap (the code comment says so), so it does not stop allocation.

5. No other guard applies. The model can be changed at any time from SettingsView.swift:39 with `Task { switchModel }`, even mid-load. DWQ (9.60 GB) plus GPTQ-small (10.45 GB) is about 20 GB, which is over the jetsam limit of a 16 GB iPad.

The proposed fix holds. | fix: In reconcileSelection(), move the cancelled task into a `draining: Task<ModelContainer, Error>?` field instead of dropping it. In load(), before starting a new performLoad, take `draining` under the lock and run `_ = try? await draining?.value`. Then call `MLX.Memory.clearCache()` and run fit() and performLoad. Optionally, also add `try Task.checkCancellation()` between weight files in the vendored loader, so a cancelled read stops early.

UPHELD(high): I confirmed the claim against origin/inkling2. Here is the failing sequence.

1. The user picks a model in SettingsView.swift (onChange, around line 36). That calls `backend.switchModel`, which calls `reconcileSelection()`. Under the lock, `reconcileSelection()` (MLXBackend.swift:66-78) does three things: it calls `inflight?.task.cancel()`, sets `inflight = nil`, and runs `epoch += 1`. The old Task's handle is now gone.

2. The old Task is still in the weight phase. In the vendored Load.swift, async `loadWeights` wraps the synchronous `loadWeights` in `withCheckedThrowingContinuation` and runs it on `DispatchQueue.global(qos: .userInitiated)`. That path runs `loadModelCheckpoint`, which uses `DispatchQueue.concurrentPerform` and `eval` per byte range, then `applyCheckpoint` and `materializeModelForInference`. None of these check `Task.isCancelled` or call `Task.checkCancellation`. So cancelling the Task has no effect, as the code's own comment admits: "a weight read finishes and is dropped". The old weights keep becoming resident until the read completes.

3. `ChatView.task(id: selectedModelID)` (ChatView.swift:57) restarts. `isLoaded` is false, so it calls `backend.load`. At MLXBackend.swift:86, `inflight` is nil, so no entry matches the new epoch, and a new `performLoad` Task for the new target starts immediately. Nothing waits for the old Task to finish. `NodeService.ensureLoaded` and a first chat message take the same path.

4. Inside the new `performLoad`, `MemoryBudget.fit` computes `budget = os_proc_available_memory() + heldByModel()`, where `heldByModel = activeMemory + cacheMemory` (MLXBackend.swift:25). Whatever the stale load has made resident lowers `available` and raises `heldByModel` by the same amount. The budget therefore stays about the same and the check passes. The same thing happens in `loadLarge` (line 134), where the soft `memoryLimit` is set from the same inflated sum. That limit is documented as soft and cannot make a load fail.

5. If the second model has already been downloaded, both weight reads run at once. On a 16 GB iPad, 9.6 GB plus 10.45 GB (about 20 GB) is well past the jetsam limit, so iOS kills the app. If the new model still needs downloading, the old read may finish first, so the crash window is narrower but still real. The PR's stated guarantee that two 10 GB loads can't run at once does not hold after a switch.

Severity high: the app is killed by jetsam, though no data is lost. | fix: In `reconcileSelection`, keep the cancelled Task as `draining = inflight?.task` instead of only dropping it. In `load()`, before creating a new `performLoad` Task, wait for the old one to finish with `_ = try? await draining?.value`, then set `draining = nil` and call `MLX.Memory.clearCache()`. To avoid holding the lock while awaiting, chain it into the new Task instead: `Task { _ = try? await prev?.value; MLX.Memory.clearCache(); try Task.checkCancellation(); return try await self.performLoad(...) }`. Only after that should `fit()` and the `memoryLimit` math in `loadLarge` run, so `heldByModel` no longer counts a load that is still in flight. Optionally, also skip `heldByModel` in `fit()` while a draining load is active.

title: The fork adds ChatSession prompt checkpoints (not in 3.33.0) that make full KV copies; for Inkling's rotating caches this adds up to ~0.9 GB that the 1.5 GiB headroom doesn't account for
scenario: This changes behavior even though it compiles. Upstream commit 4daac236 (#716), which is in 5507b3b but not in 3.33.0, records a `turn` and a `step` checkpoint on each user and tool turn whenever kvCache.needsCheckpoint is true. needsCheckpoint is true when any leaf is not trim-only. Inkling2.newCache builds a CacheList(RotatingKVCache, ConvolutionStatesCache) for every visit. With the app's maxKVSize = 8192, the global visits are RotatingKVCache(8192) too, so every leaf takes the .copy strategy. copyForCheckpoint() runs materializedCacheState, which is a real take() copy, not a shared view. A tool-calling chat near 8K tokens therefore holds the live KV (~0.43 GB by the PR's own estimate) plus up to two checkpoint copies (~0.86 GB). Restoring calls `copy.copy()`, so for a moment there is a fourth copy. That is ~1.3 GB of KV before prefill scratch, Metal overhead and the app itself, against the 1.5 GiB headroom the gate reserves. The DWQ and alt tiers can be gated as fitting and still be killed by jetsam mid-conversation. For the existing LFM2/LFM2.5 models this only copies their small conv ArraysCache, so the impact there is minor.
evidence: ChatSession.swift:1742-1760 records the checkpoint when `generateParameters.prefill.chunking == .balanced` (the default), `draftKVCache == nil` and `kvCache.needsCheckpoint`. KVCachePlan.swift:419 is `needsCheckpoint`, true when `strategies.contains { $0 != .trim }`. checkpoint() saves `.copy((leaf.cache as? RotatingKVCache)?.copyForCheckpoint() ...)`. KVCache.swift:1212 is `new.keys = new.keys.map(materializedCacheState)`, and materializedCacheState is `take(input, MLXArray(0 ..< input.dim(0)), axis: 0)`. The compare 3.33.0...5507b3b shows this code as newly added.
fix: Add 2x the KV footprint for contextTokens to `needed` for the Inkling entries (or raise headroomBytes to about 2.5 GiB), or turn checkpoints off for this app. For example, set `params.prefill.chunking` to a non-.balanced mode for Inkling if its prefill quality allows, or patch ChatSession so it skips checkpoints when the cache is rotating and memory-gated. Record the change in VENDORED.md.
notes:
UPHELD(medium): I checked every link in the claimed path on origin/inkling2, and each one can actually execute.

1. **The app goes through ChatSession.** MLXBackend.swift:170-191 sets `params.maxKVSize = contextTokens`, which is 8192 for every Inkling tier (ModelCatalog.swift:81), and builds a `ChatSession`. It never changes `prefill.chunking`, which defaults to `.balanced` (PrefillParameters.swift:75). It sets no draft model. Tool results come back as `Chat.Message.tool` through `streamDetails(to: messages)` (MLXBackend.swift:208-211), so `answering == .tool` holds on every tool step.

2. **Inkling's caches all take the copy strategy.** `Inkling2.newCache` (MLXVLM/Models/Inkling2.swift:1891-1902) builds `CacheList(attention, ConvolutionStatesCache)`. The attention cache is a `RotatingKVCache`: from `makeSlidingWindowKVCache` on sliding layers, and from `makeAttentionKVCache` on global layers, which returns a rotating cache because `maxKVSize` is set. `KVCacheLeaf.kind` (KVCacheTree.swift:22-31) maps `ArraysCache` (the convolution cache's superclass) to `.recurrent` and `RotatingKVCache` to `.rotating`. Both get `checkpointStrategy == .copy` (KVCacheTree.swift:41). Nothing is `.unsupported`, so `needsCheckpoint` is true (KVCachePlan.swift:419-423).

3. **The checkpoint is a real copy, not a view.** `checkpoint()` calls `RotatingKVCache.copyForCheckpoint()`. That function materializes keys and values through `materializedCacheState` (KVCache.swift:1212-1213), and the checkpoint is then `asyncEval`'d. That is a real allocation the same size as each leaf's live cache.

4. **Checkpoints are kept.** `Checkpoints.record` stores a `turn` checkpoint and a `step` checkpoint (ChatSession.swift:253-259). `keep(prefixing:)` keeps them for as long as the cached tokens still start with them.

**Correction to the magnitude.** The `turn` checkpoint is recorded only for a user message whose turn is prefilled fresh or rewinds the cache (`!reusesCachedPrefix || rewinds`). An ordinary follow-up user turn that appends to the reused prefix records no new one. In a typical chat the turn checkpoint is taken once, at roughly the length of the system prompt, tool specs and first message, and then persists. The step checkpoint moves to the current length on every tool step.

So in a tool-calling chat near 8K tokens, the realistic extra memory is about 1x the live KV (~0.4 GB by the app's own comment at MemoryBudget.swift:8) plus a smaller turn checkpoint. That is less than the full ~0.86 GB the claim states, which is the worst case. Restore uses `copy.copy()`, which slices with `[.ellipsis]`, so it does not necessarily allocate a fourth copy.

Even so, `headroomBytes` (1.5 GiB) is described as covering KV, prefill scratch, Metal overhead and the app. It does not count a second copy of the KV held for the whole conversation, so the memory gate underestimates real use by roughly 0.4-0.8 GB for Inkling. The path is real; whether it actually triggers jetsam depends on the device's real `os_proc_available_memory`, which I could not measure. Severity medium stands. | fix: In MemoryBudget.fit, add an extra KV term for entries that use rotating caches (Inkling): about 1-2x the KV footprint at contextTokens (~0.4-0.9 GB). Alternatively, raise headroomBytes to about 2.5 GiB for the Inkling tiers. Another option is to disable checkpoints for Inkling by setting params.prefill.chunking to a non-.balanced mode in MLXBackend.makeConversation and MLXBackend+Node, if Inkling's prefill quality allows it, and to record this in VENDORED.md.

UPHELD(medium): I couldn't refute the mechanism. Everything below was checked on origin/inkling2:
- Inkling2.newCache (MLXVLM/Models/Inkling2.swift:1891) builds a CacheList for each layer visit. Each list holds an attention cache (a sliding-window cache, or makeAttentionKVCache as? RotatingKVCache, which is rotating because the app sets maxKVSize=8192) plus a ConvolutionStatesCache.
- KVCacheTree.checkpointStrategy (KVCacheTree.swift:39) maps .rotating and .recurrent to .copy. So needsCheckpoint (KVCachePlan.swift:419) is true for Inkling. Nothing in the app turns it off: MLXBackend.swift:166-193 and MLXBackend+Node.swift:13-19 set only maxKVSize, prefill.stepSize, temperature and maxTokens. Prefill chunking stays at the default .balanced (Evaluate.swift:368 says "prefill now defaults to balanced chunking").
- ChatSession.swift:1746-1760 arms a checkpoint for every tool turn and for any user turn that rewinds or does not reuse the cached prefix. defaultGeneration then records it in Checkpoints, which holds a `turn` and a `step` slot (ChatSession.swift:228-262), so two can be live at the same time.
- KVCachePlan.checkpoint() calls RotatingKVCache.copyForCheckpoint() (KVCache.swift:1202-1214). That applies materializedCacheState, a take() gather (KVCache.swift:8-11), to keys and values. It is a real copy, sized to the current cache contents (up to the 8K global and window-sized sliding rows).
- So a long tool-calling Inkling chat holds the live KV (~0.43 GB, the app's own estimate in MemoryBudget.swift:8-9) plus up to two copies of about that size (~0.86 GB).
- MemoryBudget.fit (MemoryBudget.swift:10, 60-70) reserves a flat 1.5 GiB for KV, prefill scratch, Metal overhead and the app, and does not count this extra.
- MLX.Memory.memoryLimit in loadLarge is a soft cap (the code comment says so). It does not stop allocations, so it does not prevent jetsam.

One part of the claim is overstated. The "fourth copy on restore" is not a lasting extra. Restore calls copy.copy(), and RotatingKVCache.copy() uses `$0[.ellipsis]`, which is a view, not a gather. The old live cache is replaced at that point. The extra memory is therefore about 2x the live KV, not 3x.

I could not prove an actual jetsam kill without a device. The concrete defect is that the memory gate does not account for this extra KV. A model can pass the gate as fitting and then go over its limit during a long tool-using conversation. | fix: Account for the checkpoint copies in the memory gate. For entries whose contextTokens is set and whose cache is rotating or recurrent (the Inkling tiers), add about 2x the 8K KV footprint (~0.9 GB) to `needed` in MemoryBudget.fit. A simpler option is to raise headroomBytes to about 2.5 GiB for those entries. The alternative is to turn checkpoints off for Inkling: set params.prefill.chunking = .remainder in makeConversation and in MLXBackend+Node for Inkling entries, and confirm that this does not affect prefill correctness or tool-step rewinds, which would then fall back to a full rebuild. Either way, record the decision in VENDORED.md. There is no need to model a third copy at restore time.

UPHELD(medium): I checked each link in the claim on origin/inkling2 and every one holds.

1. Inkling2.newCache (MLXVLM/Models/Inkling2.swift:1891-1903) builds a CacheList for every layer visit. Sliding visits get makeSlidingWindowKVCache, which returns a RotatingKVCache. Global visits get makeAttentionKVCache, which returns a RotatingKVCache when a capacity is set (CacheConfiguration.swift:317-322). The app always sets one: the catalog's inkling() helper uses contextTokens 8192, and MLXBackend.swift:170 and MLXBackend+Node.swift:15 copy it into params.maxKVSize. Each visit also gets a ConvolutionStatesCache.

2. In KVCacheTree.swift:39-46, the .rotating and .recurrent leaves use the .copy strategy. needsCheckpoint (KVCachePlan.swift:419-424) is therefore true for every Inkling cache.

3. The app changes only prefill.stepSize and never chunking. The default is .balanced (PrefillParameters.swift:75). The guard at ChatSession.swift:1749-1755 passes for text-only user and tool turns with no draft cache, so checkpointPosition gets set.

4. TokenIterator produces prefillCheckpoint, which is recorded into Checkpoints (ChatSession.swift:228-261). That store keeps up to two at once: `turn` and `step`. A tool reply replaces `step`, and a user turn replaces `turn` and clears `step`. In a tool-calling chat both are alive together.

5. KVCachePlan.checkpoint() calls RotatingKVCache.copyForCheckpoint() (KVCache.swift:1202-1214) on every rotating leaf. That function ends with materializedCacheState, a take() that allocates new buffers rather than a shared view. Each checkpoint is therefore a real copy of the KV at its own prefix position. The two copies are bounded by the live cache size, so together they come to at most twice the live KV.

6. Restore (KVCachePlan.swift:405) returns copy.copy(). For RotatingKVCache that copy is a `[.ellipsis]` view, so it adds little until the next write. The "fourth copy" in the claim is overstated, but this does not change the main point.

7. MemoryBudget.headroomBytes is 1.5 GiB, and its own comment budgets only "~0.4 GB at 8K" of KV for Inkling 2. fit() adds only resident weights plus that headroom. Nothing accounts for the up-to-two extra KV copies that this fork's vendored ChatSession now retains.

Result: a long tool-calling Inkling conversation can hold about 0.43 GB of live KV plus up to about 0.86 GB of checkpoints, before prefill scratch and app overhead. The gate's estimate is wrong by close to 1 GB, so a tier gated as fitting can still hit jetsam mid-conversation.

Two uncertainties remain. The exact figures depend on the real KV size, which I took from the app's own 0.43 GB estimate; sliding-window layers are smaller, and the turn checkpoint usually sits at a shorter prefix than the live cache. How close the device runs to its limit also depends on os_proc_available_memory, which I could not measure. So the size of the overshoot is approximate, but the missing accounting is real. Medium severity is reasonable. | fix: In MemoryBudget.fit, add a per-entry KV allowance for entries that use rotating caches (Inkling): about 3x the KV footprint at contextTokens, covering the live cache plus the turn and step checkpoints. A simpler option is raising headroomBytes to about 2.5 GiB for Inkling entries.

The other option is to switch checkpoints off for Inkling. Setting params.prefill.chunking to a non-.balanced mode would do it, if prefill quality allows. Patching the vendored ChatSession to skip checkpoint recording when it is memory-gated would also work.

Whichever is chosen, record the change in ios/Vendor/VENDORED.md. The "fourth copy on restore" part of the claim should be dropped: RotatingKVCache.copy() makes a view, not a materialized copy.

title: maxKVSize=8192 makes Inkling's global-attention layers rotating caches that keep only 4 tokens, so long chats silently evict the system prompt and tool specs
scenario: Inkling2.newCache uses `makeAttentionKVCache(parameters:) as? RotatingKVCache ?? DirectAttentionKVCache()` for the global visits. When maxKVSize is set, makeAttentionKVCache returns capacity.makeRotatingCache with preservedPrefixTokens defaulting to 4. A tool-using agent conversation, where file or web tool results add thousands of tokens, passes 8192 tokens. The global layers then drop everything except the first 4 tokens and the most recent ~8188. That includes the system instructions, the tool schemas and any guard text. Nothing errors, and the app has no truncation or summarization (no contextTokens use outside GenerateParameters), so the model keeps producing answers without its instructions or tool definitions. Tool-call quality degrades, and instructions that injected content was meant to be checked against are lost. Before this PR no entry set maxKVSize, so this is a new behavior. The PR describes 8192 only as a memory cap.
evidence: ModelCatalog.inkling(...) sets `contextTokens: 8192`. MLXBackend.swift:170 has `if let context = current.contextTokens { params.maxKVSize = context }`. CacheConfiguration.swift:318 is `if let capacity = try parameters?.effectiveKVCacheCapacity() { return capacity.makeRotatingCache(...) }`, and KVCacheConfiguration.swift:58 is `init(maxTokens: Int, preservedPrefixTokens: Int = 4)`. A grep for contextTokens/truncat in ios/AgentConsole finds no history trimming.
fix: Enforce the budget at the app layer. Count the rendered prompt's tokens (the tokenCount helper already exists) and trim or summarize old turns so instructions and tools plus history stay under contextTokens. Alternatively, use the kvCache capacity API with preservedPrefixTokens set to the system and tools prefix length. At minimum, show a 'context full, start a new chat' warning instead of evicting silently.
notes: UPHELD(high): I checked every cited link on origin/inkling2 and each one holds. (1) ModelCatalog.swift:81: `inkling(...)` sets `contextTokens: 8192` for all three Inkling tiers. (2) MLXBackend.swift:170 (chat) and MLXBackend+Node.swift:15 (fleet node) both run `if let context = ...contextTokens { params.maxKVSize = context }`. On origin/integration, `git grep maxKVSize|contextTokens` under ios/AgentConsole finds nothing, so this behavior is new in the PR. (3) KVCachePlan.swift:550-599: with no typed kvCache, `effectiveKVCacheCapacity()` resolves the legacy maxKVSize to `Capacity(maxTokens: 8192, preservedPrefixTokens: min(4, 8191)) = 4`. (4) CacheConfiguration.swift:317-322: `makeAttentionKVCache` returns `capacity.makeRotatingCache(...)` whenever a capacity exists, and KVCachePlan.swift:536 builds `RotatingKVCache(maxSize: 8192, keep: 4, ...)`. (5) Inkling2.swift newCache (~line 1893): for non-sliding (global) layer visits it uses `makeAttentionKVCache(parameters:) as? RotatingKVCache ?? DirectAttentionKVCache()`. The cast succeeds, so the global layers get a rotating cache with keep=4. The attention kernels (Inkling2.swift ~984/997) read `rotating?.preservedPrefixTokens` and pass `evicted: offset+1-keys.dim(2)`, so the model is built to handle eviction rather than fail on it. Nothing errors, and only 4 prefix tokens are kept. (6) ChatSession holds one generateParameters/cache for the whole conversation. In the app, the only hits for contextTokens, maxKVSize, truncate or tokenCount are the two param assignments and NodeService's tokenCount, which only reports a count. So no history trimming, budget check or 'context full' warning exists. Reaching 8192 tokens is realistic: each turn can use up to 2048 generated tokens on thinking models, on top of the system prompt, tool schemas and tool results. After that, the system instructions and tool specs drop out of the global-attention context with no signal. Severity medium is reasonable: there is no crash, but tool calling and instructions degrade silently, and guard text against prompt injection is lost. This affects both chat and fleet-node conversations. | fix: Keep the 8192 memory cap, but stop the eviction being silent. Option A: before each turn, count the rendered prompt with `container.encode` (the tokenCount helper already exists). When instructions + tools + history + maxTokens would pass contextTokens, start a fresh ChatSession that re-sends the instructions and tools with trimmed or summarized history, and show a 'context full, older turns dropped' notice. Option B: pass `params.kvCache = KVCacheConfiguration(capacity: .init(maxTokens: 8192, preservedPrefixTokens: <token length of system+tools prefix>))` instead of maxKVSize, so the instructions are pinned. Option B still drops middle history silently, so it should also come with a UI warning.

The sliding layers already had their own window, so after the cap no layer can see the system prompt or tool schemas.
5. I found no guard. A grep of ios/AgentConsole for contextTokens, truncat, trim, tokenCount and prefix/suffix found no history trimming, no budget check and no 'context full' warning. tokenCount is used only in NodeService.swift:310 for stats. The vendored ChatSession.swift has no maxKVSize or overflow handling.

A tool-using chat with file or web results can plausibly pass 8192 tokens, and then the instructions and tool specs are evicted with no error. Medium severity is reasonable, since this is quality loss and loss of guard text rather than a crash. Removing the cap is not a fix by itself, because an unbounded cache risks jetsam on a 16 GB iPad. | fix: Keep the 8192 memory cap, but stop it from evicting silently. When a conversation is created, count the tokens in the rendered system and tools prefix (MLXBackend.tokenCount already exists). Then either (a) pass a capacity with preservedPrefixTokens equal to that prefix length, using KVCacheConfiguration.Capacity(maxTokens: 8192, preservedPrefixTokens: prefixLen) through the kvCache capacity API instead of the bare maxKVSize, or (b) track the session's running token count in MLXConversation. When the next turn would go past contextTokens, rebuild the ChatSession with the instructions, the tools and a trimmed or summarized history, or show a 'context full, start a new chat' error. At minimum, show that warning instead of rotating silently.

UPHELD(high): I traced the whole chain on origin/inkling2 and could not refute the claim.

1. ModelCatalog.swift:81: the Inkling entry sets `contextTokens: 8192`. The field is documented as "KV-cache capacity in tokens (`maxKVSize`)". No entry on origin/integration uses contextTokens, so this behavior is new.
2. MLXBackend.swift:170 (and MLXBackend+Node.swift:15): `if let context = current.contextTokens { params.maxKVSize = context }`.
3. Inkling2.newCache: the global (non-sliding) layers use `try makeAttentionKVCache(parameters:) as? RotatingKVCache ?? DirectAttentionKVCache()`. The sliding layers use makeSlidingWindowKVCache.
4. CacheConfiguration.swift: in makeAttentionKVCache, a set effectiveKVCacheCapacity leads to `capacity.makeRotatingCache(...)`. The doc for KVCacheConfiguration.Capacity says this "bounds the remaining attention layers", and `init(maxTokens:, preservedPrefixTokens: Int = 4)` keeps only 4 prefix tokens. The Inkling attention code reads `rotating?.preservedPrefixTokens` and `evicted: offset + 1 - keys.dim(2)`, which confirms that eviction is real, not just a nominal setting.
5. The conversation keeps growing across turns. LocalAgent stores one `conversation` (a ChatSession with a persistent KV cache) and reuses it for every user turn and every tool-result turn (up to 4 tool steps per message). It is cleared only by reset() or invalidateConversation(). Each assistant turn may generate up to 2048 tokens, since Inkling has thinks=true. Tool results are added in full: nothing in ios/AgentConsole truncates them (no prefix/maxChars caps on tool output). The only token counting is tokenCount, used for NodeService stats.

Failing scenario: a user has a multi-turn chat with Inkling, with a few 2K-token thinking replies plus a document or tool result, and the total passes 8192 tokens. The global-attention layers then keep only tokens 0-3 plus the most recent ~8188. The system instructions, tool list and file list from instructions(), plus the tool schemas in the chat-template prefix, are evicted from global attention. The sliding layers had already lost them. Nothing throws, and the app shows no warning. The model keeps answering without its instructions or tool definitions, so tool-calling quality degrades and the "worker jobs need approval" framing is lost. That framing is only advisory, though: confirmation is still enforced in Swift by tools.execute and confirm.

The cap is a deliberate memory trade-off, which is why the severity is medium rather than high. The silent loss of instructions is still a real defect in the behavior. I found no trimming or summarization layer that would mitigate it. | fix: Keep the memory cap but stop the silent eviction. In LocalAgent.run, before each send, estimate how many tokens the conversation holds: track the prompt and generated token counts from the stream info, or call MLXBackend.tokenCount on the rendered history. When the next turn would go past contextTokens minus a margin (maxTokens + 512), start a fresh conversation. Call makeConversation again with the same instructions and tools, and seed it with a short summary or the last N turns. Surface a 'context full, started a new chat' turn in the UI. Another option is to build params.kvCache with `KVCacheConfiguration(capacity: try .init(maxTokens: 8192, preservedPrefixTokens: <token length of the rendered system + tools prefix>))` so the instruction prefix is pinned in the global layers. At minimum, show an error turn instead of evicting silently.

title: A cancelled stale load clears the new load's pending-load breadcrumb and overwrites the last-load report
scenario: Load A (Inkling tier 1) is cancelled by a switch mid-read and keeps running (see the first finding). Load B for tier 2 sets memory.pendingLoad. Load A then finishes and runs `defaults.removeObject(forKey: pendingLoadKey)`, and also writes its own lastLoadReport. If jetsam then kills the app during B, noteLaunch() finds no pending key. The 'previous launch died mid-load' warning never appears, and Settings shows A's report as the last load.
evidence: loadLarge unconditionally does `defaults.set("\(target.id) at ...", forKey: pendingLoadKey)` at line 138, `defaults.removeObject(forKey: MemoryBudget.pendingLoadKey)` at line 151 and `defaults.set(report, forKey: lastLoadReportKey)` at line 159, with no epoch check.
fix: Pass startEpoch into loadLarge. Clear the breadcrumb and write the report only if the epoch is still current, or only if the pending value equals the string this load wrote.
notes:
UPHELD(high): I could not refute this. I checked it against origin/inkling2.

How the stale load keeps running:
- reconcileSelection (MLXBackend.swift:66-78) cancels the inflight task, clears `inflight` and bumps `epoch`.
- The comment at line 72 says a weight read in progress "finishes and is dropped". So task A can get past `VLMModelFactory.shared.loadContainer` (line 145) after a switch.
- Load B can start at the same time: after the switch, `load()` (lines 85-91) sees `inflight == nil` and creates a new task. That task's performLoad calls loadLarge for the new target.

What loadLarge does with no epoch check:
- Line 138 sets `memory.pendingLoad`.
- Line 151 removes it.
- Line 159 writes `memory.lastLoadReport`.

So the race works as claimed. B writes the breadcrumb, then A's weight read completes and A removes B's breadcrumb and writes its own report. If jetsam then kills the app during B's load (a likely moment, since two big loads may be resident together), MemoryBudget.noteLaunch (MemoryBudget.swift:41-45) finds no pending key. The "died mid-load" diagnosis is lost, and SettingsView.swift:127 shows A's report.

The epoch guard at line 95 only stops A's container from being installed. It does not cover these UserDefaults side effects. The impact is diagnostics only, so low severity is right. If A is cancelled during the download, it throws before line 151 and does no harm. The bug needs A to be in the weight-read phase, which the code itself says can happen. | fix: In loadLarge, save the breadcrumb string in a local (`let crumb = "..."`) and set it. After the load, clear it only if it is still this load's value: `if defaults.string(forKey: MemoryBudget.pendingLoadKey) == crumb { defaults.removeObject(...) }`. Write lastLoadReport only if this load's epoch is still current. To do that, pass startEpoch through performLoad and check `lock.withLock { epoch == startEpoch }`. Alternatively, call `try Task.checkCancellation()` right after loadContainer returns and before either write. A cancelled stale load then throws without touching the defaults.

UPHELD(medium): I could not refute this. I checked origin/inkling2 MLXBackend.swift.

How the race happens:
- `reconcileSelection` (lines 66-78) cancels the inflight task, sets `inflight = nil` and bumps `epoch`. Its own comment at line 72 says a weight read "finishes and is dropped". So stale load A can keep running.
- A new `load()` then sees `inflight == nil` (line 86) and starts load B, which runs its own `performLoad` and then `loadLarge`.
- `loadLarge` (lines 125-161) has no epoch or identity check. B sets the pending key at line 138. If A's `loadContainer` returns after that, A removes the key unconditionally at line 151 and writes its own report at line 159.
- The epoch check exists only in `load()` at line 95. That check decides whether A's container is kept. It does not cover the UserDefaults side effects.

What this breaks:
- If jetsam then kills the app during B, nothing on disk shows a load was in progress, so the "previous launch died mid-load" warning is lost.
- Settings shows A's stale report as the last load. If B later finishes, it overwrites that report, so only the crash case keeps the wrong report.

Why it stays low severity:
- It only affects the diagnostics breadcrumb and report.
- A has to survive cancellation, which the comment says happens during the weight-read phase. If A throws `CancellationError` instead, line 151 is never reached and there is no bug.
- B has to get past `MemoryBudget.fit` while A is still alive.

This is exactly the case where jetsam is most likely, because two models are in memory, so losing the breadcrumb there matters. | fix: Make the breadcrumb owned by the load that wrote it:
1. In `loadLarge`, store the written string, e.g. `let token = "\(target.id) at ..."`.
2. Write it with `defaults.set(token, forKey: pendingLoadKey)`.
3. After `loadContainer`, clear the key only when `defaults.string(forKey: pendingLoadKey) == token`.
4. Write `lastLoadReport` only when that same check holds, or when the epoch is still current.

Alternatively, pass `startEpoch` into `performLoad`/`loadLarge` and skip both writes when `lock.withLock { epoch } != startEpoch`.

UPHELD(high): I could not refute this. Every step of the scenario holds on origin/inkling2.

1. There are three .vlm Inkling tiers (ModelCatalog.swift, `inklingTiers`), and all of them go through loadLarge. Switching from one tier to another is a normal user action.
2. reconcileSelection (MLXBackend.swift:66-78) cancels `inflight.task`, sets `inflight = nil` and bumps `epoch`. Its own comment says a weight read "finishes and is dropped".
3. The vendored MLXLMCommon load path has no `Task.checkCancellation` or `isCancelled` checks. A grep found them only in generation and other code, not in factory loading. So when load A is cancelled during the weight read, VLMModelFactory.loadContainer returns normally and loadLarge keeps going.
4. `inflight` is now nil, so the next load() for tier 2 starts a new Task (B). B's loadLarge sets `memory.pendingLoad` at line 138 while A is still reading weights.
5. When A finishes, it calls `defaults.removeObject(forKey: pendingLoadKey)` at line 151 with no epoch or ownership check. That deletes B's breadcrumb. A then writes its own report at line 159. The epoch guard at line 95 only stops A's container from being installed; it does not protect these UserDefaults writes.
6. If jetsam kills the app while B is still loading, MemoryBudget.noteLaunch finds no pendingLoadKey. No killedLoad is recorded, so the "previous launch died mid-load" warning never appears. SettingsView:127 shows A's lastLoadReport, which describes a stale tier.

The damage is limited to diagnostics: the breadcrumb and the report. No model or user data is lost, so severity low is right. | fix: In loadLarge, keep the exact breadcrumb string the load wrote, for example `let crumb = "\(target.id) at ..."`. After the load, remove the key only if `defaults.string(forKey: pendingLoadKey) == crumb`. Write lastLoadReport only if that check passed. Another option is to pass startEpoch into performLoad and loadLarge, and do the clear and the report write only inside `lock.withLock { epoch == startEpoch }`.
